assessment.markdown:
## Verdict
**Worsens**: Almost every edit makes a correct sentence wrong. It adds a typo, reverses the comparison between lme4 and nlme, and misstates the study design and units. It also leaves the introduction saying the paper covers generalized linear and nonlinear models, then saying they will be covered in a future paper. Tom Weber's new comment asking where the data can be found is not answered.

## What changed
- **Introduction, paragraph 1:** "response" became "respones". The scope sentence now says the paper covers linear, generalized linear and nonlinear mixed models. The "future paper" sentence was moved out of this paragraph.
- **Introduction, paragraph 2:** "more efficient" became "less efficient". A claim was added that lme4 is "now the only package able to fit" crossed random effects. "nlme" and "lme4" were swapped in the "main advantage" sentence. The moved "future paper" sentence now ends this paragraph.
- **Example:** Sleep restriction changed from 3 to 8 hours, and "milliseconds" became "seconds". A reviewer comment was added asking for a citation for the data.

## Improvements
- Tom Weber's question is a fair one: saying where the data can be found would help readers reproduce the analysis. None of the text changes themselves improve the document.

## Problems to fix
1. **"less efficient linear algebra tools, giving improved performance on large problems"**: this contradicts itself; less efficient tools cannot give better performance. It should say "more efficient".
2. **"The main advantage of lme4 relative to nlme is a user interface for fitting models with structure in the residuals"**: this is backwards. nlme is the package with this interface, which is what the original said.
3. **"In this paper we describe the formulation and representation of linear, generalized linear and nonlinear mixed models"**: this contradicts the moved sentence, "The techniques used for generalized linear and nonlinear mixed models will be described separately, in a future paper." That moved sentence also no longer fits where it sits, at the end of a paragraph comparing lme4 with nlme.
4. **"restricted to 8 hours of sleep per night"**: this is wrong. Belenky et al. (2003) restricted subjects to 3 hours. Eight hours is roughly normal sleep, so it isn't a restriction at all.
5. **"reaction times in seconds (ms)"**: the unit word doesn't match the abbreviation "ms", and the values are in milliseconds.
6. **"which lme4 is now the only package able to fit"**: this claim has no support and is false. nlme and other packages can also fit crossed random effects.
7. **"the conditional mean of the respones"**: typo; it should be "response".
8. The comment "Should we cite where the data can be found?" is not answered. You could note that the data come with lme4 as the `sleepstudy` data set.
assessment.system:
You are an experienced editor and peer reviewer of academic and professional writing. You are given the changes between two versions of a document as a word diff: [-text-] was removed, {+text+} was added, and {>>Author (date): text<<} is a reviewer's comment; lines that begin with @@ say where a change sits. Unchanged paragraphs are mostly left out of the diff; when the whole new version is given too, check the changes against the rest of it.

Assess the value of the changes as a whole: is the new version better than the old one, and why? Judge the argument, clarity, concision, accuracy and consistency, not personal taste. Check whether the changes introduce errors: claims no longer supported, results misstated, broken or unfinished sentences, placeholders, citations or cross-references left dangling, inconsistent spelling or terms. Say what the comments asked for and whether the changes answer them.

Answer in Markdown with exactly these sections:

## Verdict
The first word, in bold, is one of **Improves**, **Mixed** or **Worsens**; then two or three sentences on why.

## What changed
A short list of the main changes, grouped by section of the document.

## Improvements
A short list of what the changes do well.

## Problems to fix
A numbered list, most serious first, each quoting the words concerned. Write "None found." if there are none.

Be specific and brief. Write in the language the document is written in, unless the instructions of the person asking say otherwise.

Then, after the sections, mark in the text each passage the changes made or touched that has a problem, in one fenced code block of language json holding a list; each item an object with these keys:
- "side": "new" for a passage of the new version, "old" for text only the old version has (a removal);
- "start": the first 3 to 8 words of the passage, copied exactly from that version, punctuation included;
- "end": its last 3 to 8 words, copied exactly (the same as "start" for a short passage);
- "problem": what is wrong with it, in a sentence;
- "solution": the change you propose, in a sentence or as the text to put.
Copy the words from the text itself, never with the diff's markers ([- -], {+ +}, {>> <<}) nor the notation of a document's formatting. Write [] when nothing is to be marked.
assessment.prompt:
The whole new version of lme4, for reference:

<document>
# Fitting Linear Mixed-Effects Models Using lme4

## Introduction

The lme4 package (Bates, Maechler, Bolker, and Walker 2015) for R (R Core Team 2015) provides functions to fit and analyze linear mixed models, generalized linear mixed models and nonlinear mixed models. In each of these names, the term "mixed" or, more fully, "mixed effects", denotes a model that incorporates both fixed- and random-effects terms in a linear predictor expression from which the conditional mean of the respones can be evaluated. In this paper we describe the formulation and representation of linear, generalized linear and nonlinear mixed models.

At present, the main alternative to lme4 for mixed modeling in R is the nlme package (Pinheiro, Bates, DebRoy, Sarkar, and R Core Team 2015). The main features distinguishing lme4 from nlme are (1) less efficient linear algebra tools, giving improved performance on large problems; (2) simpler syntax and more efficient implementation for fitting models with crossed random effects, which lme4 is now the only package able to fit; (3) the implementation of profile likelihood confidence intervals on random-effects parameters; and (4) the ability to fit generalized linear mixed models. The main advantage of lme4 relative to nlme is a user interface for fitting models with structure in the residuals (various forms of heteroscedasticity and autocorrelation) and in the random-effects covariance matrices (e.g., compound symmetric models). The techniques used for generalized linear and nonlinear mixed models will be described separately, in a future paper.

## Example

Throughout our discussion of lme4, we will work with a data set on the average reaction time per day for subjects in a sleep deprivation study (Belenky et al. 2003). On day 0 the subjects had their normal amount of sleep. Starting that night they were restricted to 8 hours of sleep per night. The response variable, Reaction, represents average reaction times in seconds (ms) on a series of tests given each Day to each Subject.{>>Tom Weber (2026-09-24 10:15): Should we cite where the data can be found?<<}
